items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And that was run by Steiffel, Sam Steiffel.

ctx.x: This is 1932. And we were stranded in Philadelphia. In fact, the story of Philadelphia is a crack up. We had played all these places and stranded from place to place. So finally we're getting into Philadelphia and we're going to play the Pearl Theater. And that was run by Steiffel, Sam Steiffel. Now we're going to play there a week. We'd never had a week stand any place. So we were going to play there a week with chorus girls, and they had this Ristina Banks (PHONETIC) number one chorus there playing with us.

But now, the night we got into Philly, we were going to open the next day, Fletcher Henderson's band was rehearsing there to go to New York. And that's when I first came face to face with Coleman Hawkins. And I was so thrilled, you know, to see Coleman Hawkins in person. And we -- so anyway, we opened there that next day. And we were so happy that we were going to get a week's salary at the end of the week we just had a ball, you know, we would tab our room, we'd tab food, tab our whiskey. We was having a ball…
